item.title: Reps to probe 22 States over unpaid pensions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the failure of 22 states to pay retirement benefits regularly, following concerns that thousands of elderly pensioners are being abandoned to hunger, poverty and preventable deaths. The resolution was sequel to a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Adesola Adebayo, representing Apapa Federal Constituency of Lagos State, on Tuesday at plenary. Moving the motion, Rep. Adebayo cited a report indicating that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states pay pensions regularly, while the remaining 22 owe retirees several months or, in some cases, several years of entitlements. He described pensions as an earned right rather than a privilege or charity, stressing that retirees who had devoted between 30 and 35 years to public service deserved to enjoy their benefits without unnecessary hardship. The lawmaker expressed concern that many pensioners aged between 70 and 90 were dying in poverty because they could not afford food, medication, rent and other basic necessities. He also raised concerns over the practice of subjecting elderly retirees to prolonged verification exercises, forcing some to queue for days under harsh weather conditions, with reports of pensioners collapsing and dying in the process. Adebayo argued that the non-payment of pensions amounted to a violation of constitutional provisions and human dignity, while creating fear among serving public workers who could begin to see retirement as a death sentence. The motion, however, generated disagreements among lawmakers over the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to intervene in pension matters involving state governments. Rep. Mark Essiet opposed the motion, arguing that state pension obligations fell within the jurisdiction of state governments and their respective Houses of Assembly. He cautioned against any suggestion that the Federal Government should deduct money from states’ allocations to settle outstanding pension liabilities, describing such an approach as unconstitutional. Umoh urged the House to concentrate on the pension challenges facing military personnel, who, he said, had repeatedly protested over their entitlements. Similarly, Rep. Dominic Okafor cautioned against generalising the allegations against all states, noting that some governors had fulfilled their pension obligations. He cited Anambra State as an example, arguing that the motion should distinguish between states that had failed to pay and those that were meeting their responsibilities. But Rep. Billy Owasaro urged the House not to abandon the motion, proposing amendments to remove provisions outside its constitutional jurisdiction. He argued that the suffering of elderly pensioners was too serious for lawmakers to ignore. Owasaro said: “We know what our fathers are going through. item.title: A vote for Tinubu will translate into preservation of the North – Shettima
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has called on the people of the North to vote massively for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu on January 16, 2027. Shettima made the call on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi during the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Rally, held at Haliru Abdu Stadium in Kebbi. The vice president stated that a vote for President Tinubu and VP Shettima would be a vote for the preservation of the North. “We are grateful that the North kept its promise in 2023. The North repaid Tinubu’s kindness and support for late former President Muhammadu Buhari. “We are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in January 2027. You have rejected the lies, the distortions. “And the half-truths, the taunts, the insinuations, the threats and the noise of the opposition. We are here because you can see through them. “A vote for His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, and for me as your Vice President is a vote for the preservation of the North,” he said. On security, Shettima said President Tinubu increased the salaries of the armed forces by up to 80 per cent and prioritised the welfare of all security agencies. “He also understands the needs of our farmers. Thousands of you participated in our dry-season programme to grow rice, maize and cassava. “That is why we have continued to supply you with the equipment you need. “Of the superhighway we are building from Sokoto to Badagry to ease movement across the country, 258 kilometres run through Kebbi. That is the longest stretch in any state,” the VP added. Shettima said Tinubu’s administration also undertook repairs on the Jega-Koko-Yauri and Birnin Kebbi-Argungu federal roads to ease journeys. “But roads alone are not enough without electricity. “We have increased the capacity of the Birnin Kebbi transmission substation while constructing a 3.5-megawatt solar project in Ambursa to serve homes and businesses,” he said. On healthcare, he said the Renewed Hope administration of Tinubu upgraded the Federal Medical Centre in Birnin Kebbi to a teaching hospital. “While primary healthcare centres across the state receive federal support through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund. “We have also invested in the skills of your young people. “Mr. President’s economic reforms have increased the revenue available to states to fund their initiatives and projects,” Shettima revealed. The Vice President said that Kebbi, like other states, struggled to fund its projects. He assured that the administration would not rest until every kobo earned and saved through “these reforms is invested in your welfare. “This is why we have come again: to continue what we started about three years ago. “On 16 January 2027, I trust you to come out en masse and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On 6 February 2027, I trust you to return Gov. Nasir Idris for a second term. We have so much to do to fix this country, and we must all do our part,” he said. The post A vote for Tinubu will translate into preservatio

item.description: Says President Tinubu Presides oover Opaque N11,2 trillion Pipeline Security bill that Doubles the Entire military budget while Starving of Armed Forces, Security continues to escalate By Henry Umoru ABUJA- The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC has the alarm that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is presiding over what it termed, an opaque N11.2 trillion pipeline security expenditure, alleging that the amount exceeds Nigeria’s entire defence and security budget. According to the party, the figure was contained in the audited financial disclosures of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), which reportedly showed N11.2 trillion in “other receivables from the Federation” linked to energy security costs and what it described as unverified off-budget deductions. The NDC while calling for what it described as an immediate forensic audit of the ₦11.2 trillion NNPCL energy security balance to establish the amounts paid to private contractors and those arising from legacy deductions, also asked for full disclosure of funds released for military capital equipment and troop welfare in 2025 and 2026. Ikokwu who questioned the reason for the expenditure at a time when insecurity, including kidnapping, killings and ransom payments, continues to threaten communities across the country, alleged that the huge pipeline security bill raised questions about transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, describing the expenditure as a possible political patronage fund disguised as energy security. item.title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of Kebbi Inland Dry Port
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state. The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital. He also pledged to approve additional road infrastructure projects for the state following requests by Governor Nasir Idris. The rally, held at the Birnin Kebbi Stadium, attracted thousands of APC supporters who gathered to express their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders were also present at the event, which featured speeches and goodwill messages from party chieftains. ﻿ Speaking at the rally, Governor Idris expressed satisfaction with the turnout and pledged that Kebbi State would deliver 100 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in the 2027 election. Also addressing the crowd, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulazeez Yari, said the President had done much for the North-West, including Kebbi State. Yari attributed the large turnout to Tinubu’s acceptance in the region, citing the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway project, which he said would pass through more than 200 kilometres of Kebbi State. In his remarks, Shettima urged residents of the North to support Tinubu’s re-election, recalling the President’s support for the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who governed Nigeria for eight years. He said Tinubu had stood by Buhari during his political journey and throughout his administration. Taking the podium, Tinubu thanked the people of Kebbi for their support and commended Governor Idris for his leadership. He subsequently announced the approval of some federal projects requested by the governor, including the establishment of the Kebbi Inland Dry Port. The rally also featured goodwill messages from the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy President of the Senate and other APC leaders and supporters. item.title: ‎FG launches CNG stations in four varsities
item.description: By Chidi Ndaa ‎TO ease the transport challenges of varsity students, staff and host communities, the Federal Government on Tuesday inaugurated Compressed Natural Gas Stations in four universities. The CNG stations are located at the University of Uyo (Akwa Ibom State), University of Nsukka (Enugu State), Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun (Delta State), and the University of Calabar (Cross River State). ‎The Minister of State, Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the scheme was aimed at ensuring that students, staff and members of the host communities enjoyed cheap transportation to their various destinations. Ekpo, who launched the scheme at UNIUYO, added that CNG was generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, offering motorists within the communities the opportunity to spend less on cleaner fuel. The minister hailed President Bola Tinubu for his (Tinubu) Renewed Hope Agenda, which has placed natural gas at the heart of the country’s economic renewal programme. Ekpo disclosed that the President had also approved the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation Programme. According to him, the programme is in line with the 20 Universities CNG Ecosystem Initiative to mitigate the effect of petroleum subsidy reform on students and staff. He said, “For students, young people who earn a living from commercial transport, and vulnerable members of society who depend on public transport, these savings mean lower transport costs and more money kept in their pockets for education, enterprise, food and other household needs.” “The benefits of adopting CNG for mobility are practical and immediate. CNG is generally cheaper than petrol and diesel, so vehicle owners, commercial drivers and transport operators spend less on fuel. ‎“Under the watch of Mr President, gas is no longer a resource we merely flare or export; it is a resource we are using to power our vehicles, create jobs and put money back in the pockets of our people.”. Thanking the governors of Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states for deepening the penetration of natural gas in their states, Ekpo hailed the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, for backing the scheme. He pointed out that the scheme was connecting educational institutions with national energy priorities. ‎The Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, Oluwole Adama, said the newly inaugurated CNG stations in Uyo, Calabar, Enugu and Warri could fill about 540 vehicles every day. Adama said, “For students, affordable and dependable transport means more than a cheaper ride. It can mean getting to lectures on time, spending less on daily travel and having more time and energy for learning,” he said. ‎He stated that the facilities could become living classrooms that would offer young Nigerians practical exposure to gas operations, engineering, safety and maintenance. ‎He added, “About 50 more projects will be nearing commissioning by the end of this year. item.title: Single Window: Nigeria’s $6.1bn non-oil exports drive fresh trade reforms
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government on Tuesday disclosed that it is set to streamline export documentation and regulatory approvals from December 14, 2026, as part of efforts to sustain growth in Nigeria’s non-oil exports, which hit a record $6.1bn in 2025. The reform, under the second phase of the National Single Window project, is expected to eliminate multiple documentation processes, reduce bureaucratic bottlenecks and lower the cost of exporting Nigerian products. The Director of the National Single Window Project, Tola Fakolade, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ engagement in Abuja, saying the export-focused phase would provide businesses with a single digital platform for processing regulatory licences, permits and certificates. He explained that the platform would enable exporters to submit required documents through one entry point rather than visiting different government agencies to obtain multiple approvals. Fakolade said the first phase of the project, which focused on import licences and certificates, had processed more than 169,000 licences, certificates and permits since its launch. He added that feedback from users had helped improve the platform, while lessons from the import phase would guide the implementation of the export component. The initiative comes as Nigeria’s non-oil export earnings increased by 11.5 per cent to a record $6.1bn in 2025, while export volume rose by 10 per cent to 8.02 million metric tonnes. The Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council, NEPC, Nonye Ayeni, who disclosed the figures, said the country exported 281 products to 120 countries, including 36 African nations. Ayeni, however, warned that sustaining the growth would require addressing trade procedures and regulatory delays, which she identified as major challenges confronting exporters. She said exporters often had to visit several government offices, submit identical documents repeatedly and secure multiple approvals before their goods could leave the country. According to her, such delays sometimes result in contract cancellations, increased business costs and deterioration of perishable products, leading to rejection by international buyers. She said the National Single Window would address the challenges by connecting relevant government agencies to a centralised digital platform for submitting, processing and approving trade documents. Ayeni disclosed that NEPC was working with the National Single Window Secretariat to integrate its export certification registration process, currently operated through the council’s e-registration portal, into the platform. She added that the council was also working to connect its Export Expansion Grant platform through an application programming interface to facilitate seamless processing and eliminate the movement of physical documents between institutions. item.title: I contemplated suicide at height of Man United career, Rooney reveals
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated suicide during the height of his Manchester United career, despite success on the pitch and major milestones in his personal life. Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, the former England captain said he struggled with his mental health, spent two days at a time drinking at home and withdrew from people around him. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well. “I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. “I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.” Rooney, Manchester United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 goals, said he found it difficult to admit he was struggling because he feared it would be seen as a sign of weakness. “You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said. “Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that. “I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because, when I look back, I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life, and it wasn’t. “It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.” Rooney, who married Coleen in 2008 and became a father to their first child, Kai, the following year, credited his wife with helping him through the period. “Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said. Rooney left Manchester United in 2017 and later had spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County. His last managerial role was at Plymouth Argyle, which he left in December 2024. item.title: 2027: We’ll never disappoint you — Kebbi governor assures Tinubu
item.description: Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the state will remain loyal to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and deliver overwhelming support for his re-election in the 2027 presidential election. Idris gave the assurance on Tuesday while welcoming Tinubu to the state during the APC campaign rally, saying Kebbi had consistently supported the President and would do even more in the forthcoming election. “Mr President, Kebbi State has never disappointed you, and we will never disappoint you. In 2023, we gave you total support. In this election, we will give you even more,” the governor said. He added, “I assure you that Kebbi State will deliver APC 100 per cent by God’s grace.” The governor described the large turnout at the rally as evidence of the state’s support for Tinubu and his running mate, Vice-President Kashim Shettima. “This massive crowd you see here is a clear testimony that Kebbi State is APC and Kebbi State is for Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kashim Shettima,” he said. Idris also commended the President for what he described as his administration’s interventions in the state, particularly in agriculture, infrastructure, education, healthcare and security. He thanked Tinubu for the Renewed Hope Agenda and support for farmers, which he said had contributed to a rice revolution in Kebbi. “We thank you for the roads, for the schools, for the hospitals, and for security support you give us,” he said. The governor said his administration had also invested in strengthening the state’s security architecture, improving health facilities, providing free agricultural inputs to farmers and constructing rural and township roads across the state. According to him, the investments have helped farmers work with confidence, created employment opportunities for young people and supported the empowerment of women. Idris, however, used the occasion to appeal to Tinubu to facilitate the full operationalisation of the Samia Inland Dry Port in Bagoro Local Government Area of the state. He said the facility, when fully operational, would boost revenue generation, create jobs and promote economic growth in Kebbi. item.title: Super Eagles held to dissapointing goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Super Eagles of Nigeria were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania on Tuesday, missing the chance to strengthen their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Eric Chelle’s side had more possession and created several chances but could not find a way past the hosts’ defence in 90 minutes. The Super Eagles started brightly, with Moses Usor seeing an effort blocked inside the opening 15 minutes. Fisayo Dele-Bashiru also tested Tanzania with a shot from outside the penalty area, while Tolu Arokodare fired wide in the 35th minute. Tanzania remained a threat after the break, with Kibu Denis and Iddi Selemani both missing opportunities to put their side ahead. Nigeria continued to press, but Akor Adams sent an effort wide from the centre of the penalty area in the 70th minute. Arokodare later came close with a left-footed attempt from inside the box, but his shot also failed to hit the target. Tanzania nearly snatched a late winner when a speculative effort from the edge of the area struck the post. Alhassan Yusuf then tried to release a forward with a through ball, but the move was stopped for offside. Nigeria could not find a breakthrough in the closing minutes as Tanzania held on for a point. Nigeria will now hope Madagascar defeat Guinea-Bissau in Group L to keep their qualification hopes alive. Eric Chelle’s side had claimed a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf scored the opener before Tolu Arokodare struck twice after the break. The Super Eagles went into Tuesday’s match with six points from three games, one point behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who had played out a 1-1 draw with Madagascar in their previous fixture. Tanzania had already qualified for the tournament as one of the co-hosts, leaving Nigeria, Guinea-Bissau and Madagascar to battle for the group’s other qualification spot. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda will jointly host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations from June 19 to July 17. item.title: Electoral violence: Senate urges INEC to disqualify candidates over supporters’ actions
item.description: Condemns Actions, Asks State governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadia under their control for political activities It is a shame to see candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives or governorship surrounded by supporters carrying dangerous weapons, Senator Kawu By Henry Umoru ABUJA- DISTURBED by recurring cases of political thuggery and violence across the country, the Senate has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to disqualify any political candidate whose supporters are found to have instigated or participated in acts of electoral violence, irrespective of party affiliation, in accordance with the provisions of the 2026 Electoral Act and an established conviction by the court. The Senate has condemned in very strong terms escalation in the frequency and spread of political violence across the country, characterised by what it described as attacks on political leaders, supporters and political gatherings, with grave implications for National Security, democratic participation and the peaceful conduct of the 2027 General Elections. The Senate further asked state governors to stop denying opposition parties access to public facilities, including hotels and stadiums under their control, for political activities. The Senate has urged all the rrelevant security agencies to conduct impartial and transparent investigations into reported incidents of political violence in Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states, as well as other affected areas. Resolutions of the Senate on Tuesday were sequel to a motion on the urgent need to check the rising incidence of violence, intolerance and attacks on political leaders and supporters in the country sponsored by Senator Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central. Ningi’s motion came as a recent of reports of attacks on political figures, including the incident involving President Bola Tinubu at a mosque on Friday. In a robust debate, the lawmakers asked security agencies to investigate reported incidents in four states (Abuja, Edo, Delta and Sokoto states), identify the perpetrators and their sponsors and ensure prosecution. The Senate further urged the agencies to identify the perpetrators and sponsors of such incidents and ensure their prosecution in accordance with the Electoral Act 2026. It urged the Federal Government to direct the Inspector-General of Police and other relevant Security Agencies to strengthen security arrangements for political leaders, candidates, supporters and political gatherings nationwide, and establish effective early-warning and rapid-response mechanisms to prevent political violence ahead of the 2027 General Elections. item.title: Reps seek NYSC posting reforms over rising kidnapping risks
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for an urgent review of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) mobilisation and deployment policy to reduce the exposure of corps members to kidnapping, accidents and other security threats while travelling to their places of primary assignment. The call followed a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Yallema Makki, who raised concerns over the growing security risks faced by young graduates travelling across the country for their mandatory national service. The lawmaker noted that corps members were often required to travel long distances from their states of residence to their states of deployment, sometimes passing through areas affected by insecurity. He expressed concern over reported cases of corps members being kidnapped, particularly while travelling to their states of deployment or places of primary assignment. Makki warned that the dangers associated with long-distance journeys, coupled with poor road conditions and insecurity along some routes, could undermine the confidence of corps members and their families in the safety of the scheme. He emphasised that the safety and welfare of young Nigerians undertaking national service should remain a priority throughout their mobilisation, orientation, deployment and service periods. The lawmaker recalled that the NYSC was established in 1973 to promote national unity, integration, patriotism and mutual understanding among Nigerian youths through the deployment of graduates to different parts of the country. However, the he argued that the objectives of national integration could still be achieved without exposing corps members to unnecessary security risks. Makki maintained that a more flexible deployment arrangement, which takes into account geographical proximity, prevailing security conditions and identified high-risk routes, would help reduce the dangers associated with inter-state journeys. The motion further observed that posting corps members to states closer to their places of residence, where practicable, could minimise their exposure to kidnapping and road accidents without undermining the objectives of the national service programme. Consequently, the House adopted the motion and mandate its relevant committees to engage the NYSC management and other stakeholders to immediately review the existing mobilisation and deployment policy, with greater emphasis on the safety and security of corps members. It also called on the NYSC to develop a more flexible deployment framework that would allow corps members to be posted to states geographically closer to their states of residence, particularly where long-distance journeys could expose them to significant security threats. The relevant committees are also expected to monitor compliance with the proposed measures and report their findings and recommendations to the House. item.title: Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi and pleads with voters to support second-term bid
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday in Kebbi State appealed to Kebbi voters who gathered at Haliru Abdu Stadium to witness his campaign to obtain permanent voters’ cards to enable them to vote for him in the 2027 general elections. Tinubu, alongside the presidential campaign council, told Kebbi voters to support the candidature of Tinubu and his vice president, Kashi Shettima, to enable them to continue enjoying massive infrastructure already being executed in Kebbi state, which he said is evidence of federal presence. “I thank you from the bottom of my heart, the people of Kebbi State, for enduring the blazing sun to welcome me in Kebbi State. I urge you all to get your PVCs to vote for me, the governor, and other APC candidates in Kebbi State.” The president added that he was in Kebbi during the last elections; he is here again to thank Kebbi voters for their massive support in the last polls and appealed to them to do so in 2027. He pledged to continue his job in education security, healthcare and agriculture, describing it as a catalyst for food security in the country. Earlier, the presidential campaign director general of the ruling All Progressives Congress, Senator Abdul Aziz Yarima, challenged the opposition candidate to tell the people of the north what he did to them when he was at helm of affairs. Yari pointed out that Tinubu is the real lover of the north because of the massive infrastructure presence in the region. He urged the opposition in the country to reconsider their claims that Tinubu has no support in the north, saying no president in Nigeria has developed the north like president Tinubu. Yari appealed to Northwest voters not to be carried away by the lies of the opposition, who think the APC doesn’t have support in the north. In his welcome address, the governor of Kebbi state, Dr Nasir Idris, thanked the president for the presidential campaign rally in Kebbi state. He assured the president that Kebbi is for Tinubu and APC, for him as governor and all the candidates of the ruling party. “Mr President, what you are witnessing now tells you that Kebbi is for you, for APC, for me and all our candidates.” Idris pledged to deliver APC for Tinubu in the one hundred percent of the 2027 elections, saying the people of Kebbi state are eager to repay the good works of the president for the state. While commending his efforts in agriculture, security, education and healthcare, he appealed to him to grant full operation of Tsamiya inland dry port to boost economic activities in the state; the request was granted by the mister president. Kebbi rally was attended by three former Kebbi governors, serving budget minister Atiku Bagudu, APC National Chairman Netenwe, Senator Adams Oshimole, Senate President Godwill Apkabio, Speaker of the National Assembly, Abass Tajjudeen, former APC National Chairman, Vice President Kashi Shettima, Senator Remi Tinubu and top APC brass. item.title: South Africa cautions Fani-Kayode over social media remarks
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye South Africa has cautioned Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, over his social media remarks following the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa. The country’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation, DIRCO, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting between its Director-General, Zane Dangor, and Fani-Kayode. According to the statement, Dangor conveyed South Africa’s concerns over the events that followed the presentation of the Nigerian envoy’s Letters of Credence to Ramaphosa, as well as his subsequent comments on social media. The statement said, “During the meeting, the Director-General conveyed South Africa’s concern regarding events that transpired following the presentation of the High Commissioner’s Letters of Credence to His Excellency President Cyril Ramaphosa, as well as subsequent remarks made on social media.” Dangor also recalled Article 41 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving country through its Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The statement added, “Mr Dangor further recalled the provisions of Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961), which require diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving State through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. “In this regard, it was emphasised that all official communication should be conducted through established diplomatic channels, including DIRCO.” The South African department further reaffirmed the importance of preserving the longstanding bilateral relationship between both countries, founded on mutual respect, friendship and cooperation. It said, “South Africa remains committed to the continued strengthening of its strategic partnership with Nigeria and to maintaining constructive diplomatic engagement in the spirit of African solidarity and mutual respect.” Background The development follows a diplomatic controversy that erupted after Fani-Kayode presented his Letters of Credence to Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on November 13, alongside ambassadors from 14 other countries. The former minister of aviation had accused the South African presidency of deliberately excluding his introduction and speech from the official livestream of the ceremony, alleging that the broadcast cut off around the time he was scheduled to speak and resumed only after his address. In a post on his X handle, Fani-Kayode said he was the only ambassador whose introduction and speech were omitted from the broadcast, describing the development as deliberate. He also claimed that he raised the matter with Ramaphosa during a photo session after the ceremony, adding that the South African President directed relevant officials to address his complaint. item.title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate. The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes. Supporters rally for Tinubu in Katsina State. He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected. “We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.» “Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.” The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state. The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector. Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area. The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities. Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda. He charged officers of the NSCDC to uphold professionalism, diligence, and discipline in the discharge of their duties while fostering stronger collaboration with other security agencies and host communities. item.title: Senate chief whip, Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) stalwarts, have escaped Boko Haram’s attempted attack in the Kukawa Local Government Area of the state. Sources said Monguno and a former Governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan, among others, stormed Kukawa in continuation of their 2027 campaign tour. Earlier, Monguno had joined Governor Babagana Zulum at the official launch of the campaign in Monguno town last Sunday, before the governor disengaged on Monday from Monguno back to Maiduguri via a helicopter, while some of his entourage arrived in Maiduguri the same day by road. Sources said some politicians, including the Senate Chief Whip, proceeded from Monguno to Kukawa to canvass for votes, in which the terrorists attempted to dislodge the community. It was also gathered that, based on intelligence, troops of Operation Hadin Kai swung into action and foiled the attempted attacks by terrorists on the campaign entourage. According to reports by Yerwa News Express, a local online media outlet said, “The terrorists fired three mortar bombs toward Kukawa on Monday while Mr Monguno, former Borno State Governor Maina Maaji Lawan, and other political figures were in the town for campaign activities. “Local sources had earlier reported threats by the terrorists to disrupt the campaign, prompting heightened security measures. “Troops of Operation Hadin Kai detected the movement of the terrorists around Kukawa and swiftly responded, preventing them from carrying out the attack. “The campaign team subsequently returned safely to Monguno without any casualties. “The terrorists reportedly made further attempts to attack the town throughout the night but were prevented from gaining access.” In a related development, troops foiled another attempted attack on Kekeno village in the early hours of Tuesday, November 17, 2026. “At about 1:20 a.m., alert troops spotted suspicious movements by suspected terrorists travelling on foot from the general area of Barwati toward Kekeno village. “The troops immediately advanced toward the suspected terrorists and engaged them with heavy gunfire. “Unable to withstand the troops’ firepower, the terrorists reportedly fled into the surrounding bush. “The military said follow-up operations are ongoing in the area to track down the fleeing terrorists. “It added that the situation remained calm, with troops maintaining heightened surveillance.” Sources and Yerwa Express News reported. Due to a lack of telecommunication networks in the zone, the Senate Chief Whip’s phone number was not available at the time our correspondent dialled to confirm the incident. item.title: Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased. Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He wrote, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist. “I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added. “May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss. “May his soul rest in peace.” Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44, according to a statement by the management of Vanguard Media Limited. His death has continued to attract tributes from political figures, media practitioners and other Nigerians, who have mourned his passing and remembered his contributions to journalism. item.title: ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the Trade Union Congress (TUC) regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers. The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting with the Federal Government in response to a letter dated 8th October, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the Union. TUC President, Alex Osifo, in handshake with Ayo Fayose during the meeting While the meeting was chaired by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the TUC delegation was led by the President, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo, and comprised Comrade General N.A. Toro, Secretary-General; Comrade Shehu Mohammed, Deputy President; Comrade Akintola Benjamin, Trustee; and Comrade Kamal Ibrahim, Auditor II. Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, during the meeting Also in attendance were the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana. While providing further explanation, TUC noted that it had insisted on a salary increment rather than a mere one-off N70,000 six-month transportation package. “In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage. “This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee”, the statement read in part. According to the statement, the government has already attended to some of the demands raised by the TUC. “The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations”, the statement said in part. The composition of the High-Powered Committee includes three representatives from the TUC, led by the Secretary-General, Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), Permanent Secretary, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. The High-Powered Committee is expected to commence work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks. item.title: ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country. Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent. Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday. He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere. He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism. The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. “We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced. The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance. He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. item.title: British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway
item.description: By Dickson Omobola British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today. The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight. Pictures shared with The Sun showed the Boeing 787 Dreamliner stranded, with its nose wheel stuck in a grass verge. According to The Sun, emergency services raced to the scene of the stranded aircraft, which had sparked disruption at the airport. Airport sources suggested to The Sun that pilot error could have been responsible for the incident, which occurred at about 10.40am. A source told The Sun, “The packed plane was all set to go and had pushed back from its stand, taxiing to the runway for take-off to Lagos. “Bafflingly, the plane appears to have simply been driven off the tarmac onto a grass verge. It is hard to understand what could be to blame for this, other than a most basic pilot error. “There are red faces all around the airline, and a hefty task clearing up the mess and looking after hundreds of disgruntled passengers who were strapped in their seats for lift-off.” British Airways told The Sun, “We are very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right.” The post British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway appeared first on Vanguard News .
